category: Core vocabulary: weather and the sky

entries.meaning: Cloud has 3 distinct senses.
examples: A dark cloud moved in over the lake.
The clouds finally broke around noon.
You could see his breath turn into a little cloud of steam.
The truck left a cloud of dust behind it.
A cloud of smoke hung over the valley for days.
Clouds of insects rose out of the grass.
All my photos are backed up to the cloud.
The company moved its records to the cloud.
You can open the file from the cloud on any device.

senses.head: A white or gray mass of water droplets floating in the sky
examples: A dark cloud moved in over the lake.
The clouds finally broke around noon.
You could see his breath turn into a little cloud of steam.

senses.head: A mass of smoke, dust, or tiny particles floating in the air
examples: The truck left a cloud of dust behind it.
A cloud of smoke hung over the valley for days.
Clouds of insects rose out of the grass.

senses.head: Storage and computing power provided over the internet instead of on your own machine
examples: All my photos are backed up to the cloud.
The company moved its records to the cloud.
You can open the file from the cloud on any device.

entries.meaning: Sun has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The sun comes up around six this time of year.
Don't sit in the sun too long without a hat.
Some of those planets orbit two suns.
The kids were out in the sun all afternoon.
This corner of the yard gets very little sun.
Put a hat on and stay out of the sun.

senses.head: The star that the earth goes around and that gives us light and heat
examples: The sun comes up around six this time of year.
Don't sit in the sun too long without a hat.
Some of those planets orbit two suns.

senses.head: Sunlight and its warmth, thought of as something you sit in or keep out of
examples: The kids were out in the sun all afternoon.
This corner of the yard gets very little sun.
Put a hat on and stay out of the sun.

entries.русский: солнце; солнце, солнечный свет (тепло и свет)
entries.contrast: Sun and son are perfect homophones in American English.

entries.meaning: Moon has 2 distinct senses.
examples: There's a full moon tonight.
The moon was so bright we didn't need a flashlight.
Jupiter has dozens of moons.
Jupiter has dozens of moons.
Titan is the largest moon of Saturn.
The probe photographed two small moons nobody had seen before.

senses.head: The large round object that circles the earth and shines at night
examples: There's a full moon tonight.
The moon was so bright we didn't need a flashlight.
Jupiter has dozens of moons.

senses.head: A natural body that circles a planet other than the earth
examples: Jupiter has dozens of moons.
Titan is the largest moon of Saturn.
The probe photographed two small moons nobody had seen before.

entries.meaning: Star has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Out in the desert you can see thousands of stars.
That bright star is actually Venus.
We lay on the roof and counted stars.
He became a star after his first album.
The movie stars arrived in dark glasses.
She was the star of the school play.
The teacher put a gold star on her paper.
The restaurant earned three stars in the guide.
Draw a star at the top of the tree.

senses.head: A huge ball of burning gas that looks like a point of light at night
examples: Out in the desert you can see thousands of stars.
That bright star is actually Venus.
We lay on the roof and counted stars.

senses.head: A famous and successful performer or athlete
examples: He became a star after his first album.
The movie stars arrived in dark glasses.
She was the star of the school play.

senses.head: A pointed shape used as a symbol, a reward, or a rating
examples: The teacher put a gold star on her paper.
The restaurant earned three stars in the guide.
Draw a star at the top of the tree.

entries.русский: звезда; звезда (знаменитость); звезда (фигура, знак отличия, оценка)

entries.meaning: The light and warmth that come directly from the sun. ---
examples: We got two straight weeks of sunshine.
The kitchen gets great sunshine in the morning.
After all that rain, the sunshine felt amazing.

entries.meaning: Natural light from the sun. ---
examples: Keep the paint out of direct sunlight.
Sunlight was pouring through the blinds.
These plants need about six hours of sunlight a day.

entries.meaning: The light that comes from the moon at night. ---
examples: We walked back to the cabin by moonlight.
The snow looked blue in the moonlight.
There was just enough moonlight to see the trail.

entries.meaning: Ray has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A ray of sun came through the curtains.
Sunscreen blocks the rays that burn your skin.
The first rays hit the top of the mountain.
A ray glided over the sand right below us.
Rays often bury themselves in the shallows.
The aquarium has a tank where you can touch the rays.

senses.head: A narrow line of light or heat traveling from something
examples: A ray of sun came through the curtains.
Sunscreen blocks the rays that burn your skin.
The first rays hit the top of the mountain.

senses.head: A flat sea fish with wide winglike fins and a long thin tail
examples: A ray glided over the sand right below us.
Rays often bury themselves in the shallows.
The aquarium has a tank where you can touch the rays.

entries.meaning: Shade has 4 distinct senses.
examples: Let's eat in the shade — it's ninety degrees out here.
That old oak gives the whole yard shade.
There's no shade anywhere on this beach.
Pull the shades down before the sun hits that window.
She raised the shade and looked out at the street.
The lamp in the hall needs a new shade.
The wall is a darker shade of blue than I wanted.
They sell the same shirt in eight shades of gray.
Her hair had gone a lighter shade over the summer.
The two words carry different shades of meaning.
There was a shade of doubt in his voice.
Every answer came with a shade of sarcasm.

senses.head: An area that is cooler and darker because something blocks the sun
examples: Let's eat in the shade — it's ninety degrees out here.
That old oak gives the whole yard shade.
There's no shade anywhere on this beach.

senses.head: A cover pulled down over a window, or the cover over a lamp
examples: Pull the shades down before the sun hits that window.
She raised the shade and looked out at the street.
The lamp in the hall needs a new shade.

senses.head: A particular variety or depth of a color
examples: The wall is a darker shade of blue than I wanted.
They sell the same shirt in eight shades of gray.
Her hair had gone a lighter shade over the summer.

senses.head: A slight difference or a small amount of something
examples: The two words carry different shades of meaning.
There was a shade of doubt in his voice.
Every answer came with a shade of sarcasm.

entries.русский: тень (прохладное место); штора, жалюзи; абажур; оттенок (цвета); нюанс, лёгкая примесь, чуточка
entries.contrast: Russian «тень» splits in two: shade is the cool area out of the sun, shadow is the dark shape an object casts.

entries.meaning: The dark shape made on a surface when something blocks the light. ---
examples: My shadow was ten feet long by five o'clock.
The shadows got longer as the sun went down.
He stepped out of the shadow of the building.

entries.meaning: Dawn has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The crew starts work at dawn.
We drove all night and got there at dawn.
It was a cold, gray dawn.
This was the dawn of the personal computer.
The treaty promised the dawn of a new era.
Storytelling goes back to the dawn of human history.

senses.head: The first light of the day, just before the sun comes up
examples: The crew starts work at dawn.
We drove all night and got there at dawn.
It was a cold, gray dawn.

senses.head: The beginning of a period or of a new state of things
examples: This was the dawn of the personal computer.
The treaty promised the dawn of a new era.
Storytelling goes back to the dawn of human history.

entries.meaning: The dim light at the end of the day, just after sunset. ---
examples: The deer come out around dusk.
We played ball until dusk.
The streetlights come on at dusk.

entries.meaning: Twilight has 2 distinct senses.
examples: We hiked the last mile in twilight.
In summer the twilight lasts almost an hour up here.
The lake looked silver in the twilight.
He hit thirty home runs in the twilight of his career.
The novel is set in the twilight of the Roman Empire.
In the twilight of her life she took up painting.

senses.head: The soft half-light in the sky before sunrise or after sunset
examples: We hiked the last mile in twilight.
In summer the twilight lasts almost an hour up here.
The lake looked silver in the twilight.

senses.head: The last stage of something, when it is fading or coming to an end
examples: He hit thirty home runs in the twilight of his career.
The novel is set in the twilight of the Roman Empire.
In the twilight of her life she took up painting.

entries.meaning: Daylight has 2 distinct senses.
examples: We only have about two hours of daylight left.
The colors look completely different in daylight.
Try to get off the mountain while there's still daylight.
There was no daylight between the mayor and the governor on the budget.
The lead runner opened up some daylight between herself and the pack.
You could see daylight under the door where it didn't sit flush.

senses.head: The natural light of day, or the hours when it is light outside
examples: We only have about two hours of daylight left.
The colors look completely different in daylight.
Try to get off the mountain while there's still daylight.

senses.head: A gap or clear space between two people, things, or positions
examples: There was no daylight between the mayor and the governor on the budget.
The lead runner opened up some daylight between herself and the pack.
You could see daylight under the door where it didn't sit flush.

entries.русский: дневной свет; светлое время суток; просвет, зазор; расхождение (во мнениях)

entries.meaning: The time when it gets dark at the end of the day. ---
examples: They wanted to reach the campground by nightfall.
The temperature drops fast after nightfall.
The search was called off at nightfall.

entries.meaning: An event in which one body in space blocks the light of another. ---
examples: Schools closed early so kids could watch the eclipse.
There's a lunar eclipse next Tuesday night.
Total solar eclipses are rare in any one place.

entries.meaning: A statement of what the weather is expected to be. ---
examples: The forecast says rain all weekend.
Did you check the forecast before you packed?
These ten-day forecasts are never right.

entries.meaning: Climate has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Arizona has a dry climate.
My knees do better in a warm climate.
These grapes only grow in cool climates.
The political climate has changed since the election.
Small firms are struggling in the current economic climate.
A climate of fear kept people from speaking up.

senses.head: The usual weather a place has over many years
examples: Arizona has a dry climate.
My knees do better in a warm climate.
These grapes only grow in cool climates.

senses.head: The general mood or set of conditions surrounding a situation
examples: The political climate has changed since the election.
Small firms are struggling in the current economic climate.
A climate of fear kept people from speaking up.

entries.meaning: Atmosphere has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Most meteors burn up in the atmosphere.
The upper atmosphere is far colder than that.
Mars has a thin atmosphere with almost no oxygen.
The café has a warm, relaxed atmosphere.
There was a tense atmosphere in the meeting.
Candles and old photos gave the room a cozy atmosphere.

senses.head: The layer of gases surrounding a planet
examples: Most meteors burn up in the atmosphere.
The upper atmosphere is far colder than that.
Mars has a thin atmosphere with almost no oxygen.

senses.head: The mood or feeling of a place or a situation
examples: The café has a warm, relaxed atmosphere.
There was a tense atmosphere in the meeting.
Candles and old photos gave the room a cozy atmosphere.

entries.contrast: Stress the first syllable — AT-muhs-feer, unlike Russian «атмосфЕра».

entries.meaning: Season has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Fall is my favorite season.
We get all four seasons here.
Hurricane season runs from June through November.
The football season starts in September.
Hotels double their rates during the busy season.
He hit thirty home runs last season.
The third season comes out in October.
We watched a whole season in one weekend.
The show was canceled after two seasons.

senses.head: One of the four parts of the year, or a period with typical weather
examples: Fall is my favorite season.
We get all four seasons here.
Hurricane season runs from June through November.

senses.head: The part of the year when a particular sport, crop, or business is at its height
examples: The football season starts in September.
Hotels double their rates during the busy season.
He hit thirty home runs last season.

senses.head: A set of episodes of a television show released over one period
examples: The third season comes out in October.
We watched a whole season in one weekend.
The show was canceled after two seasons.

entries.русский: время года, сезон; сезон (спортивный, туристический, уборочный); сезон (сериала)

entries.meaning: Degree has 3 distinct senses.
examples: It's supposed to hit ninety degrees tomorrow.
The temperature dropped twenty degrees in an hour.
Water freezes at thirty-two degrees Fahrenheit.
She has a degree in civil engineering.
He finished his degree at night school.
Both degrees hang framed in her office.
There is a degree of risk in any investment.
To some degree, we were all responsible.
The work requires a high degree of accuracy.

senses.head: A unit for measuring temperature
examples: It's supposed to hit ninety degrees tomorrow.
The temperature dropped twenty degrees in an hour.
Water freezes at thirty-two degrees Fahrenheit.

senses.head: A qualification given by a university to a student who completes a course of study
examples: She has a degree in civil engineering.
He finished his degree at night school.
Both degrees hang framed in her office.

senses.head: The amount or extent to which something is true or present
examples: There is a degree of risk in any investment.
To some degree, we were all responsible.
The work requires a high degree of accuracy.

entries.русский: градус; учёная степень, диплом о высшем образовании; степень, мера

entries.meaning: The amount of water vapor in the air. ---
examples: It's not the heat, it's the humidity.
The humidity makes my hair frizz.
August here is ninety degrees with eighty percent humidity.

entries.meaning: Small amounts of water in the air, in the ground, or on a surface. ---
examples: There's still moisture in the soil from last night.
The bag keeps moisture out.
Wipe the moisture off the windows before it freezes.

entries.meaning: Water that falls from the sky as rain, snow, sleet, or hail. ---
examples: We've had almost no precipitation since April.
Expect some precipitation by Thursday evening.
Annual precipitation here is about forty inches.

entries.meaning: Visibility has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Visibility was down to about a hundred feet.
Flights were delayed because of poor visibility.
The fog lifted and visibility improved.
The lawsuit gave the issue national visibility.
She took the job for the visibility it would give her career.
The brand has almost no visibility outside the Northeast.

senses.head: How far you can see, given the weather conditions
examples: Visibility was down to about a hundred feet.
Flights were delayed because of poor visibility.
The fog lifted and visibility improved.

senses.head: The amount of public attention that something or someone receives
examples: The lawsuit gave the issue national visibility.
She took the job for the visibility it would give her career.
The brand has almost no visibility outside the Northeast.

entries.meaning: Barometer has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The barometer is falling, so expect a storm.
My grandfather had a brass barometer by the door.
Barometers were standard equipment on every ship.
Consumer spending is a good barometer of the economy.
Local elections often serve as a barometer of the national mood.
Ticket sales are the industry's barometer of what audiences want.

senses.head: An instrument that measures air pressure to help predict weather
examples: The barometer is falling, so expect a storm.
My grandfather had a brass barometer by the door.
Barometers were standard equipment on every ship.

senses.head: Something that shows how a situation or a public mood is changing
examples: Consumer spending is a good barometer of the economy.
Local elections often serve as a barometer of the national mood.
Ticket sales are the industry's barometer of what audiences want.

entries.meaning: A scientist who studies and predicts the weather. ---
examples: The meteorologist on Channel 4 got it right for once.
Meteorologists had been tracking the storm for days.
She trained as a meteorologist before going into TV.

entries.meaning: Front has 4 distinct senses.
examples: There's a long scratch on the front of the car.
We sat at the front of the classroom.
The front of the building is all glass.
A cold front is moving in tonight.
The front stalled over the valley and it rained for three days.
Warm fronts usually bring steady rain instead of thunderstorms.
Her grandfather was wounded at the front.
Fresh troops were sent to the eastern front.
Letters from the front took weeks to arrive.
The car wash was a front for a gambling ring.
Police say the charity was just a front.
Several fronts were set up to move the money.

senses.head: The part or side of something that faces forward
examples: There's a long scratch on the front of the car.
We sat at the front of the classroom.
The front of the building is all glass.

senses.head: The boundary between two masses of air, which usually brings a change in weather
examples: A cold front is moving in tonight.
The front stalled over the valley and it rained for three days.
Warm fronts usually bring steady rain instead of thunderstorms.

senses.head: The line along which two armies are fighting in a war
examples: Her grandfather was wounded at the front.
Fresh troops were sent to the eastern front.
Letters from the front took weeks to arrive.

senses.head: A person or business used to hide an illegal or secret activity
examples: The car wash was a front for a gambling ring.
Police say the charity was just a front.
Several fronts were set up to move the money.

entries.русский: передняя часть, фасад; атмосферный фронт; фронт (линия боевых действий); прикрытие, ширма
entries.contrast: Spelled with an o but pronounced FRUNT, rhyming with hunt.

entries.meaning: Storm has 2 distinct senses.
examples: We lost power during the storm.
A big storm is supposed to come through Friday night.
Three storms hit the coast in two weeks.
The remark set off a storm of criticism.
The bill passed after a political storm.
Her resignation caused a media storm.

senses.head: A period of violent weather with strong wind and usually rain or snow
examples: We lost power during the storm.
A big storm is supposed to come through Friday night.
Three storms hit the coast in two weeks.

senses.head: A sudden violent outburst of public feeling or trouble
examples: The remark set off a storm of criticism.
The bill passed after a political storm.
Her resignation caused a media storm.

entries.meaning: A storm with thunder and lightning, usually with heavy rain. ---
examples: A thunderstorm rolled through and knocked out the internet.
The dog hides under the bed during thunderstorms.
Afternoon thunderstorms are normal here in July.

entries.meaning: The loud noise you hear after a flash of lightning. ---
examples: The thunder woke up the whole house.
You could hear thunder off in the distance.
Count the seconds between the flash and the thunder.
entries.contrast: Thunder is uncountable: say "we heard thunder" or "a clap of thunder", never "a thunder".

entries.meaning: A bright flash of electricity in the sky during a storm. ---
examples: Lightning hit a tree in the neighbor's yard.
Get off the water when you see lightning.
There was lightning but almost no rain.
entries.contrast: Spelled lightning, with no e — lightening is a different word meaning "making lighter". It is also uncountable: "a bolt of lightning", not "a lightning".

entries.meaning: Drizzle has 2 distinct senses.
examples: It's just drizzle — you don't need an umbrella.
The game went on through a steady drizzle.
Cold drizzle is somehow worse than real rain.
Finish the salad with a drizzle of olive oil.
The cake came with a drizzle of lemon glaze.
Add a drizzle of honey to the yogurt.

senses.head: Very light rain made of fine drops
examples: It's just drizzle — you don't need an umbrella.
The game went on through a steady drizzle.
Cold drizzle is somehow worse than real rain.

senses.head: A thin stream of liquid poured over food
examples: Finish the salad with a drizzle of olive oil.
The cake came with a drizzle of lemon glaze.
Add a drizzle of honey to the yogurt.

entries.русский: моросящий дождь, морось; тонкая струйка (соуса, масла)

entries.meaning: A sudden, very heavy fall of rain. ---
examples: We got caught in a downpour on the way to the car.
The downpour flooded the intersection in minutes.
Two downpours in one afternoon washed out the trail.

entries.meaning: A single drop of falling rain. ---
examples: The first raindrops hit the windshield.
A fat raindrop landed right on my nose.
Raindrops were beading up on the fresh wax.

entries.meaning: The amount of rain that falls in a place over a period of time. ---
examples: Rainfall was well below average last year.
Heavy rainfall overnight closed two roads.
The county measures rainfall at six different stations.

entries.meaning: A curved band of colors in the sky, caused by sun shining through rain. ---
examples: There was a huge rainbow over the field after the storm.
We saw a double rainbow from the porch.
Rainbows show up whenever the sun comes out during rain.

entries.meaning: Hail has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Hail the size of quarters dented every car on the lot.
We pulled over and waited out the hail.
The storm brought wind, rain, and hail.
The car was hit by a hail of bullets.
Her proposal met a hail of criticism.
A hail of stones came down from the ridge.

senses.head: Small balls of ice that fall from storm clouds
examples: Hail the size of quarters dented every car on the lot.
We pulled over and waited out the hail.
The storm brought wind, rain, and hail.

senses.head: A large number of things thrown, fired, or aimed at once
examples: The car was hit by a hail of bullets.
Her proposal met a hail of criticism.
A hail of stones came down from the ridge.

entries.contrast: Hail is uncountable — one piece of it is a hailstone, never "a hail".

entries.meaning: A single ball of ice that falls during a hailstorm. ---
examples: A hailstone cracked the skylight.
Some of the hailstones were as big as golf balls.
He picked up a hailstone and held it in his palm.

entries.meaning: Frozen or partly frozen rain that falls in cold weather. ---
examples: The rain turned to sleet around midnight.
Driving in sleet is worse than driving in snow.
There was sleet on the steps and I almost went down.

entries.meaning: Snow that has partly melted into a wet, dirty mush. ---
examples: The sidewalks were nothing but gray slush.
My boots are soaked from all that slush.
By noon the snow had turned to slush.

entries.meaning: Snowflake has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A snowflake landed on her glove and melted.
Big wet snowflakes were coming down fast.
No two snowflakes are supposed to be alike.
He calls anyone who disagrees with him a snowflake.
The column dismissed the protesting students as snowflakes.
Don't be such a snowflake — it was a joke.

senses.head: A single piece of falling snow
examples: A snowflake landed on her glove and melted.
Big wet snowflakes were coming down fast.
No two snowflakes are supposed to be alike.

senses.head: An insulting word for someone thought to be too easily offended or too fragile
examples: He calls anyone who disagrees with him a snowflake.
The column dismissed the protesting students as snowflakes.
Don't be such a snowflake — it was a joke.

entries.meaning: A storm in which a lot of snow falls, usually with wind. ---
examples: The snowstorm shut down every school in the county.
We drove home through a snowstorm at fifteen miles an hour.
Two snowstorms in one week is a lot, even for here.

entries.meaning: An occasion when snow falls, or the amount that falls. ---
examples: The first snowfall of the year came in October.
We had a heavy snowfall overnight.
Snowfalls like that used to happen every winter.

entries.meaning: A severe snowstorm with strong wind and very poor visibility. ---
examples: The blizzard dumped two feet of snow on the city.
They were stuck at the airport for two days because of the blizzard.
My parents still talk about the blizzard of '78.

entries.meaning: Flurry has 2 distinct senses.
examples: We're expecting flurries tonight, nothing serious.
A flurry blew past the window and stopped.
There were flurries on the drive up, but nothing stuck.
There was a flurry of calls right before closing.
The announcement set off a flurry of trading.
After a few early flurries, the day went quiet.

senses.head: A brief, light fall of snow
examples: We're expecting flurries tonight, nothing serious.
A flurry blew past the window and stopped.
There were flurries on the drive up, but nothing stuck.

senses.head: A sudden short burst of activity
examples: There was a flurry of calls right before closing.
The announcement set off a flurry of trading.
After a few early flurries, the day went quiet.

entries.русский: лёгкий снегопад, кратковременный снег; шквал, всплеск (активности)

entries.meaning: A deep pile of snow formed by the wind. ---
examples: There's a snowdrift halfway up the garage door.
The plows left snowdrifts at the end of every driveway.
He stepped into a snowdrift and sank to his knees.

entries.meaning: A ball of snow packed together in your hands. ---
examples: He threw a snowball at his brother and missed.
The snow's too dry to make snowballs today.
One snowball hit the window and everybody froze.

entries.meaning: A figure of a person built out of packed snow. ---
examples: The kids built a snowman in the front yard.
Our snowman lasted about three days.
There were snowmen on half the lawns on the street.
entries.contrast: Irregular plural: one snowman, two snowmen (SNOH-men).

entries.meaning: A pointed piece of ice hanging down where water has frozen as it dripped. ---
examples: There's a three-foot icicle hanging off the gutter.
Knock those icicles down before somebody gets hurt.
An icicle broke off and shattered on the steps.

entries.meaning: A thin white layer of ice crystals, or a night cold enough to form one. ---
examples: There was frost on the windshield this morning.
The first hard frost killed the tomatoes.
Late frosts can ruin the whole apple crop.
entries.countability: countable, and uncountable as a substance

entries.meaning: Thaw has 2 distinct senses.
examples: We got a thaw in the middle of January.
The river floods every spring during the thaw.
A couple of thaws turned the yard into mud.
The visit marked a thaw in relations between the two countries.
There's been a slight thaw between the brothers.
Trade talks brought a brief thaw.

senses.head: A period of warmer weather when snow and ice melt
examples: We got a thaw in the middle of January.
The river floods every spring during the thaw.
A couple of thaws turned the yard into mud.

senses.head: An improvement in relations between people or countries that had been unfriendly
examples: The visit marked a thaw in relations between the two countries.
There's been a slight thaw between the brothers.
Trade talks brought a brief thaw.

entries.meaning: Drops of water that form on cool surfaces outdoors overnight. ---
examples: The grass was still wet with dew.
Wait for the dew to burn off before you mow.
There was dew all over the tent by morning.
entries.contrast: Americans say DOO, a homophone of do and due; the British say DYOO.

entries.meaning: Injury to the skin and flesh caused by extreme cold. ---
examples: He got frostbite on two fingers.
Cover your ears or you'll risk frostbite.
At that wind chill, frostbite sets in within minutes.

entries.meaning: Fog has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The fog was so thick I couldn't see the mailbox.
Fog rolls in off the bay almost every morning.
The bridge was closed because of fog.
I got through the whole week in a fog.
The medication left her in a mental fog.
The first months after the baby were a complete fog.

senses.head: A thick cloud of water droplets near the ground that makes it hard to see
examples: The fog was so thick I couldn't see the mailbox.
Fog rolls in off the bay almost every morning.
The bridge was closed because of fog.

senses.head: A state of confusion in which you cannot think clearly
examples: I got through the whole week in a fog.
The medication left her in a mental fog.
The first months after the baby were a complete fog.

entries.русский: туман; туман в голове, помутнение сознания

entries.meaning: A thin fog, or a fine spray of tiny water drops in the air. ---
examples: There was mist hanging over the river at sunrise.
A light mist was falling, barely enough to wet the road.
The mist burned off by nine o'clock.

entries.meaning: Haze has 2 distinct senses.
examples: There's a haze over the whole valley from the wildfires.
You could barely make out the skyline through the haze.
Summer haze makes the mountains look blue.
I got through the baby's first month in a haze.
After the surgery he spent two days in a haze of painkillers.
The whole evening is a haze — I don't even remember leaving.

senses.head: A slight cloudiness in the air from dust, smoke, or heat
examples: There's a haze over the whole valley from the wildfires.
You could barely make out the skyline through the haze.
Summer haze makes the mountains look blue.

senses.head: A state in which someone cannot think clearly
examples: I got through the baby's first month in a haze.
After the surgery he spent two days in a haze of painkillers.
The whole evening is a haze — I don't even remember leaving.

entries.русский: дымка, мгла; туман в голове, помутнение сознания

entries.meaning: Dirty, unhealthy air over a city, made of smoke and fog. ---
examples: The smog was bad enough that they told kids to stay inside.
You can see the smog sitting over the freeway.
Smog here is much worse in the summer.

entries.meaning: A form of oxygen that forms a protective layer high in the atmosphere. ---
examples: The ozone layer blocks most of the sun's harmful rays.
Ozone at ground level is a pollutant, not a good thing.
They issued an ozone alert for the whole metro area.

entries.meaning: Pollen has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The pollen count is through the roof this week.
There's yellow pollen all over my car.
My eyes water whenever the pollen gets bad.
Everything in the driveway is coated in pollen.
The pollen count is brutal this week.
Bees carry pollen from one plant to the next.

senses.head: Fine powder from plants that floats in the air in spring
examples: The pollen count is through the roof this week.
There's yellow pollen all over my car.
My eyes water whenever the pollen gets bad.

senses.head: The fine yellow powder that flowers produce in order to make seeds
examples: Everything in the driveway is coated in pollen.
The pollen count is brutal this week.
Bees carry pollen from one plant to the next.

entries.meaning: Wind has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A cold wind was coming off the lake.

Winds of forty miles an hour knocked out the power.
The fall knocked the wind out of me.
Give me a second to get my wind back.
He found his second wind on the last mile.

senses.head: Air moving across the land or the sea
examples: A cold wind was coming off the lake.
The wind took my hat halfway down the block.
Winds of forty miles an hour knocked out the power.

senses.head: The ability to breathe normally, especially during hard effort
examples: The fall knocked the wind out of me.
Give me a second to get my wind back.
He found his second wind on the last mile.

entries.contrast: The noun is WIND (rhymes with pinned); the verb to wind a clock is WYND (rhymes with find).

entries.meaning: Breeze has 2 distinct senses.
examples: There's a nice breeze on the porch.
The breeze off the ocean keeps it from getting too hot.

With the new software, payroll is a breeze.
The hike looked hard, but it was a breeze.

senses.head: A light, pleasant wind
examples: There's a nice breeze on the porch.
The breeze off the ocean keeps it from getting too hot.
Evening breezes make August almost bearable.

senses.head: Something that is very easy to do
examples: The final exam turned out to be a breeze.
With the new software, payroll is a breeze.
The hike looked hard, but it was a breeze.

entries.русский: лёгкий ветер, ветерок; лёгкое дело, пустяк

entries.meaning: A sudden strong rush of wind. ---
examples: A gust blew the umbrella off the table.
Gusts up to sixty miles an hour are expected.
One good gust and the whole tent came down.

entries.meaning: A very strong wind. ---
examples: A gale was blowing straight off the water.
The forecast has gales along the whole coast.
They canceled the ferry because of the gale.

entries.meaning: A very large, violent tropical storm with extremely strong circling winds. ---
examples: The hurricane is expected to make landfall Thursday.
They boarded up the windows before the hurricane.
Three hurricanes hit the Gulf that season.
entries.contrast: Stress the first syllable, HUR-uh-kayn, and pronounce the last syllable fully — unlike Russian «ураган».

entries.meaning: A hurricane that happens in the western Pacific. ---
examples: The typhoon forced them to cancel the flight.
A typhoon had wiped out the docks the year before.
Typhoons are most common there in late summer.

entries.meaning: A large system of winds spinning around a center of low pressure. ---
examples: A cyclone was forming off the coast.
The cyclone brought a week of rain.
Tropical cyclones get their energy from warm ocean water.

entries.meaning: An informal American word for a tornado. ---
examples: A twister took the roof clean off the barn.
They spotted a twister about two miles out.
Twisters come through this county every spring.

entries.meaning: A seasonal wind that brings months of heavy rain. ---
examples: The monsoon usually starts in early July.
They lost the crop when the monsoon came late.
Monsoons dump most of the region's yearly rain.

entries.meaning: How cold the air feels on your skin once the wind is taken into account. ---
examples: It's ten degrees, but the wind chill makes it feel like twenty below.
Watch the wind chill before you send the kids out.
The wind chill was the story on every newscast that night.

entries.meaning: An unpleasant feeling of cold in the air or in your body. ---
examples: There's a chill in the air tonight.
Grab a jacket — you'll catch a chill out there.
The morning chill is gone by ten.

entries.meaning: A stretch of unusually hot weather lasting several days or more. ---
examples: We're in the middle of a heat wave.
The heat wave broke on Sunday night.
Two heat waves in one summer is unusual for Seattle.

entries.meaning: A short period of unusually cold weather. ---
examples: That cold snap in April killed the blossoms.
We're getting a cold snap this weekend.
A couple of cold snaps like that and the pipes will freeze.

entries.meaning: Warmth has 2 distinct senses.
examples: You could feel the warmth coming off the sidewalk.
We stepped inside for a little warmth.
Wool keeps its warmth even when it's wet.

There was no warmth in his voice at all.
I still remember the warmth of that welcome.

senses.head: The pleasant quality of being warm
examples: You could feel the warmth coming off the sidewalk.
We stepped inside for a little warmth.
Wool keeps its warmth even when it's wet.

senses.head: Friendliness and kind feeling toward other people
examples: She greeted every guest with real warmth.
There was no warmth in his voice at all.

entries.meaning: A dangerous condition caused by the body getting far too hot. ---
examples: Two runners were treated for heatstroke.
Never leave a dog in the car — heatstroke happens fast.
Dizziness and confusion are warning signs of heatstroke.

entries.meaning: Red, sore skin caused by too much time in the sun. ---
examples: I got a nasty sunburn on the boat.
His sunburn peeled for a week.
Sunburns that bad can do real damage.
entries.contrast: Americans usually say "I got a sunburn", counting it; the British more often say "I got sunburn", with no article.

entries.meaning: The warmest season of the year, between spring and fall. ---
examples: We spend every summer at my aunt's place.
It was the hottest summer on record.
She waited tables for three summers to pay for school.

entries.meaning: Fall has 4 distinct senses.
examples: The leaves are beautiful here in the fall.
She starts law school this fall.
We've had some cold falls lately.
She broke her wrist in a fall on the ice.
He took a bad fall off the ladder.
Most falls at home happen in the bathroom.
The report showed a sharp fall in unemployment.
A steady fall in prices hurt local growers.
Falls in temperature overnight can ruin the crop.
The class spent a week on the fall of the empire.
The fall of the city ended the war.
His fall from power took less than a month.

senses.head: The season between summer and winter, when leaves change color
examples: The leaves are beautiful here in the fall.
She starts law school this fall.
We've had some cold falls lately.

senses.head: An act of dropping to the ground, usually by accident
examples: She broke her wrist in a fall on the ice.
He took a bad fall off the ladder.
Most falls at home happen in the bathroom.

senses.head: A drop in the amount, level, or price of something
examples: The report showed a sharp fall in unemployment.
A steady fall in prices hurt local growers.
Falls in temperature overnight can ruin the crop.

senses.head: The loss of power by a government, or the capture of a city
examples: The class spent a week on the fall of the empire.
The fall of the city ended the war.
His fall from power took less than a month.

entries.русский: осень; падение; падение, снижение (цен, уровня); падение, крушение (власти, города)
entries.contrast: Americans normally say fall; the British say autumn. Both are understood in the US.

entries.meaning: The season between summer and winter; the more formal American word for fall. ---
examples: The poem is set in late autumn.
Autumn in New England draws tourists from everywhere.
He painted the same hillside over several autumns.
entries.contrast: The final n is silent: AW-tuhm. It comes back only in the adjective autumnal (aw-TUM-nuhl).

entries.meaning: The coldest season of the year, between fall and spring. ---
examples: Winter here lasts about five months.
We got through the winter on firewood alone.
He's lived through sixty Minnesota winters.

entries.meaning: Either of the two days in the year with the longest or shortest daylight. ---
examples: The summer solstice falls on June 21st this year.
After the winter solstice the days start getting longer.
The stones line up with the sun on both solstices.

entries.meaning: Either of the two days a year when day and night are about equal in length. ---
examples: The fall equinox is around September 22nd.
Storms are common near the equinox.
The two equinoxes mark the start of spring and fall.

entries.meaning: A large round body in space that moves around a star. ---
examples: Mars is the fourth planet from the sun.
There are eight planets in our solar system.
They think that planet may have water.

entries.meaning: The earth seen as a whole, or a round model of it. ---
examples: The company has offices all over the globe.
There was a dusty globe on the teacher's desk.
Old globes still show countries that don't exist anymore.

entries.meaning: Universe has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The universe is still expanding.
Nobody knows how big the universe actually is.
Some physicists argue for a whole set of parallel universes.
The show takes place in the same universe as the comics.
In the universe of college sports, that's a huge salary.
The two movies belong to completely different universes.

senses.head: All of space and everything in it
examples: The universe is still expanding.
Nobody knows how big the universe actually is.
Some physicists argue for a whole set of parallel universes.

senses.head: A particular world of activity, or the whole imagined world of a story
examples: The show takes place in the same universe as the comics.
In the universe of college sports, that's a huge salary.
The two movies belong to completely different universes.

entries.русский: вселенная; мир, вселенная (сфера деятельности; вымышленный мир)

entries.meaning: A huge group of stars, gas, and dust held together by gravity. ---
examples: Our galaxy has a few hundred billion stars.
The telescope picked up galaxies nobody had seen before.
That smudge of light is another galaxy.

entries.meaning: A body of ice and dust that travels around the sun and grows a bright tail. ---
examples: The comet should be visible just after sunset.
That comet only comes back every seventy-six years.
Comets pick up their tails as they get close to the sun.
entries.contrast: Don't confuse it with the verb commit: the noun is KAH-mit, stressed on the first syllable; commit is kuh-MIT.

entries.meaning: A piece of rock from space that burns as a streak of light in the sky. ---
examples: We saw a meteor go right across the sky.
The meteor shower peaks around two in the morning.
You can count twenty meteors an hour out here.

entries.meaning: A piece of rock from space that reaches the ground without burning up. ---
examples: A meteorite punched a hole in somebody's garage roof.
The museum has a meteorite you're allowed to touch.
Most meteorites found on earth are mostly iron.

entries.meaning: A small rocky body that orbits the sun, much smaller than a planet. ---
examples: An asteroid passed closer to us than the moon.
Most asteroids sit in a belt between Mars and Jupiter.
They named the asteroid after her.

entries.meaning: Orbit has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The satellite is in a low orbit.

It completes sixteen orbits a day.
Several small nations remain in Moscow's orbit.
He drifted out of our orbit after college.
The startup was pulled into the orbit of a much bigger firm.

senses.head: The curved path one object takes around another in space
examples: The satellite is in a low orbit.
The moon's orbit isn't a perfect circle.
It completes sixteen orbits a day.

senses.head: The area of influence or control that a person or country has
examples: Several small nations remain in Moscow's orbit.
He drifted out of our orbit after college.

entries.meaning: An object placed in orbit around a planet, or a moon that orbits naturally. ---
examples: The weather satellite sends back new images every ten minutes.
We get our internet by satellite out here.
There are thousands of satellites up there now.

entries.meaning: Constellation has 2 distinct senses.
examples: That constellation is easy to find in winter.
My dad taught me a few constellations when I was a kid.
The app tells you which constellation you're looking at.
The doctor looked at the whole constellation of symptoms before deciding.
A constellation of small startups has grown up around the university.
The album brought together a constellation of guest singers.

senses.head: A group of stars that people picture as forming a shape
examples: That constellation is easy to find in winter.
My dad taught me a few constellations when I was a kid.
The app tells you which constellation you're looking at.

senses.head: A group of related people or things that appear together
examples: The doctor looked at the whole constellation of symptoms before deciding.
A constellation of small startups has grown up around the university.
The album brought together a constellation of guest singers.

entries.meaning: The curved shape of the moon when only a thin part of it is lit. ---
examples: There was a thin crescent low in the western sky.

entries.contrast: The sc in the middle is a single /s/ sound: KRES-uhnt, not "kres-KENT".

entries.meaning: An instrument that makes distant objects look closer, used for looking at the sky. ---
examples: He got a telescope for his twelfth birthday.

entries.meaning: The scientific study of stars, planets, and space. ---
examples: She's taking astronomy as an elective.
Astronomy got a lot easier once we had good telescopes.

entries.contrast: Don't mix it up with astrology (uh-STRAH-luh-jee), the business of horoscopes — astronomy is the science.

entries.meaning: A scientist who studies stars, planets, and space. ---
examples: An astronomer at the university spotted it first.

entries.meaning: A person trained to travel and work in space. ---
examples: Every kid in that class wanted to be an astronaut.

entries.meaning: A vehicle built to travel in space. ---
examples: The spacecraft docked without any trouble.

entries.contrast: The plural does not change: one spacecraft, three spacecraft — like aircraft.

entries.meaning: A vehicle or device pushed upward by burning fuel, used to reach space. ---
examples: The rocket lifted off right on schedule.
They're testing a new rocket next month.
Those rockets can be flown back and reused.

entries.meaning: Gravity has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Gravity on the moon is about a sixth of what it is here.
You don't notice gravity until you try to carry something heavy.
Their bones weaken without gravity.
He didn't grasp the gravity of the charges.
Her voice made the gravity of the news clear.
The gravity of the moment silenced the room.

senses.head: The force that pulls objects toward each other, and things toward the earth
examples: Gravity on the moon is about a sixth of what it is here.
You don't notice gravity until you try to carry something heavy.
Their bones weaken without gravity.

senses.head: The serious or dangerous nature of a situation
examples: He didn't grasp the gravity of the charges.
Her voice made the gravity of the news clear.
The gravity of the moment silenced the room.

entries.meaning: A building with telescopes, used for studying the sky. ---
examples: The observatory is open to the public on Friday nights.

Several observatories tracked the same object.

entries.meaning: Hemisphere has 2 distinct senses.
examples: It's winter here and summer in the southern hemisphere.
That plant only grows in the northern hemisphere.

The stroke damaged the right hemisphere.
The two hemispheres are joined by a thick band of nerve fibers.

senses.head: One half of the earth, divided north and south or east and west
examples: It's winter here and summer in the southern hemisphere.
That plant only grows in the northern hemisphere.

senses.head: One of the two halves of the brain
examples: Language is handled mostly by the left hemisphere.
The stroke damaged the right hemisphere.
The two hemispheres are joined by a thick band of nerve fibers.

entries.meaning: Bands of colored light that appear in the night sky near the poles. ---
examples: We drove north hoping to see the aurora.

Strong solar storms can push auroras much farther south.

entries.meaning: A star together with all the planets and other bodies orbiting it. ---
examples: Neptune is at the far edge of our solar system.
The kids built a model solar system out of foam balls.
They've found thousands of other solar systems.

entries.meaning: The distance light travels in one year, used for measuring space. ---
examples: That star is about four light-years away.

entries.contrast: It measures distance, not time, even though the word year is in it.

entries.meaning: A region in space with gravity so strong that not even light can escape it.
examples: There's a black hole at the center of our galaxy.

Black holes form when very large stars collapse.
